newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab League expects Israel normalisation frozen.
newsitem.headline: Arab League expects Israel normalisation frozen.

text.p: The head of the Arab League said on Thursday he expected most Arab states to shut offices in Israel in response to a call to freeze normalisation with the Jewish state.
"The trend is to shut these offices," Esmat Abdel-Meguid, secretary general of the 22-member league, told reporters. He declined to give details but it does not apply to Jordan and Egypt.
"This recommendation was taken unanimously by all foreign ministers who attended the meeting, and according to the Arab League charter, they are binding to all".
Arab foreign ministers recommended after a meeting in Cairo on Monday that member states stop normalising ties with Israel and restore their economic boycott of Israel.
The call came in response to the Israeli government's decision to go ahead with a Jewish housing settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The recommendation affects Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia -- states which have swapped low-level offices with Israel under Middle East peace moves since 1994 -- and Qatar and Oman, which host Israeli trade missions.
It does not affect Jordan and Egypt -- the only Arab states to sign peace treaties with the Israel -- or the Palestinians whose 1993 peace deal with Israel fostered hopes for a new Middle East.
Qatar and Oman had forged ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel but have stopped short of full diplomatic ties pending comprehensive Arab-Israeli peace.

Earlier, Abdel-Meguid and the EU's special Middle East envoy, Miguel Moratinos, addressed the opening session of a conference on Euro-Arab cooperation for the peace process in Dubai. They expressed concern over renewed violence.
Israel was not invited to the Dubai meeting.
